subject: microbiology
title: VISA, Coagulase-Negative Staphylococci, S epidermidis and S saprophyticus

steps.tx: **VISA** (vancomycin intermediate S aureus, MIC 4 to 8) thickens its cell wall with extra peptidoglycan decoy targets that soak vancomycin before it reaches the membrane, emerging under prolonged glycopeptide exposure in MRSA bacteraemia and deep foci, while fully resistant VRSA (MIC 16 plus) borrows vanA from enterococci rarely. Disc diffusion cannot detect VISA; MIC methods must.
steps.say: A thicker wall sponges vancomycin mid journey; only MIC testing catches VISA.

left.title: VISA mechanics
points: Thickened wall, increased free D Ala D Ala decoys
Vancomycin trapped and clogged in outer layers
Selected by prolonged exposure and undrained foci

right.title: Detection and response
points: Broth MIC or gradient methods (no disc)
Reference confirmation and infection control alert
Daptomycin and linezolid alternatives by syndrome
Source control is the decisive therapy

steps.tx: **VISA**, vancomycin intermediate Staphylococcus aureus, has a minimum inhibitory concentration of 4 to 8. Extra peptidoglycan thickens the wall and soaks vancomycin up as a decoy before the drug reaches the membrane. Prolonged glycopeptide treatment of MRSA bacteraemia, especially with an undrained focus, selects this state. VRSA, minimum inhibitory concentration 16 or higher, is rarer and borrows vanA from enterococci. Disc diffusion misses VISA. Only an MIC method catches the thickened wall phenotype.
steps.say: VISA means a vancomycin minimum inhibitory concentration of 4 to 8. A thicker wall full of peptidoglycan binds the drug before it reaches its membrane target, usually after long glycopeptide courses for MRSA with a deep focus. VRSA, at 16 or more, instead borrows vanA from enterococci. Disc tests miss VISA, so an MIC method is required.

vis.alt: An electron micrograph shows a thickened staphylococcal cell wall crowded with extra peptidoglycan.
vis.caption: Extra peptidoglycan thickens the wall so vancomycin binds decoy targets before it reaches the membrane site of action. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Staphylococcus epidermidis** heads the coagulase negative staphylococci (CoNS): skin commensal turned device pathogen by biofilm (polysaccharide intercellular adhesin), contaminating blood cultures innocently far oftener than it infects, yet the leading cause of prosthetic valve endocarditis early, line infections, CSF shunt and prosthetic joint infections where it is isolated repeatedly.
steps.say: One bottle epidermidis is skin; the same organism in three sets on a prosthesis is disease.

left.title: Device pathogen
points: Biofilm on lines, valves, joints, shunts
Indolent, weeks of low grade symptoms
Multiple positive sets with identical pattern

steps.tx: **Staphylococcus saprophyticus** (novobiocin resistant CoNS) causes honeymoon cystitis, urinary infection in young sexually active women second to E coli in that group, adhering to uroepithelium, D serine deaminase armed, usually susceptible to urinary agents, and identified when a CoNS in urine is not dismissed as contamination in a symptomatic young woman.
steps.say: A CoNS in a young woman's urine is saprophyticus until proven otherwise.

right.title: Urine CoNS triage
points: Symptomatic young woman: treat as pathogen
Catheterised or elderly mixed growth: caution
Speciation worth it in recurrent cases
Staph aureus in urine hints bacteraemia separately

steps.tx: **CoNS identification** sorts the skin crowd: novobiocin susceptibility (epidermidis susceptible, saprophyticus resistant), haemolysis, urease, ornithine and sugar patterns, MALDI now naming lugdunensis, the CoNS that behaves like aureus (aggressive endocarditis, abscesses) and must never be waved away as contaminant. Species identification therefore matters most in blood, joint fluid, prosthesis sonicate and cerebrospinal fluid, where a name changes both drug choice and decisions about removing hardware.
steps.say: Lugdunensis wears a CoNS coat with an aureus heart; name it and respect it.

left.title: Bench sorting
points: Lugdunensis: PYR and ornithine clues, MALDI confirms
Capitis, haemolyticus, hominis line and NICU niches

right.title: Clinical weight by species
points: Others: context decides, speciation in sterile sites

steps.tx: **Biofilm mechanics** unite the device lessons: attachment, accumulation (PIA polysaccharide or protein mediated), maturation with channels, dispersal seeding downstream, antibiotic tolerance by depth and dormancy exceeding resistance by orders, rifampicin's biofilm activity (never alone, resistance) and device removal as the reliable cure.
steps.say: Tolerance by architecture beats resistance by gene on devices; remove or suppress forever.

steps.tx: **Biofilm** forms by attachment, accumulation in a polysaccharide or protein matrix, maturation with fluid channels, and dispersal of cells downstream. Tolerance from depth and dormancy, not a resistance gene, is why antibiotics fail by large margins. Rifampicin reaches staphylococcal biofilm better than many drugs and must never be given alone, or resistance is prompt. Taking the device out is the dependable cure. Lifelong suppression is what remains if removal is impossible.
steps.say: Device biofilm attaches, builds a polysaccharide or protein matrix, matures channels, then sheds cells downstream. Dormant cells deep in the film tolerate antibiotics far beyond ordinary resistance. Rifampicin has biofilm activity in staphylococci but breeds resistance if used alone. Removal of the device is the cure that drugs cannot match.

vis.alt: An electron micrograph shows bacteria embedded in a matrix on a catheter surface, with channels running through the film.
vis.caption: Bacteria embedded in a matrix coat the catheter, with channels through the film and cells at the surface ready to disperse. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Blood culture contamination** discipline protects patients from CoNS overtreatment: contamination rates benchmarked (under 3 percent), skin antisepsis and diversion devices lowering them, interpretation rules (sets positive, time to positivity, device presence) taught to every prescriber, vancomycin days saved by restraint counted by stewardship.
steps.say: Every contaminated set costs days of vancomycin and a line of false history; draw clean.

left.title: Contamination prevention
points: Chlorhexidine alcohol skin prep, dry fully

steps.tx: **Methicillin resistance in CoNS** exceeds even MRSA rates (mecA widespread in skin flora), narrowing device therapy to glycopeptides and successors empirically until susceptibilities return, while making CoNS a resistance gene reservoir for aureus on shared skin. Device prophylaxis and lock therapies (antibiotic and ethanol locks) live in this reality.
steps.say: Skin staphylococci are a mecA library aureus borrows from; empiric device cover assumes it.

left.title: CoNS resistance
points: mecA in majority of hospital CoNS
Vancomycin empiric for serious device infection
Linezolid and daptomycin by site and duration

right.title: Prevention echoes
points: Line bundles cut CoNS CLABSI too
Antimicrobial lock prophylaxis in selected lines
Stewardship de escalates on culture patterns

steps.tx: **Neonatal and neurosurgical niches** close the CoNS file: late onset neonatal sepsis leaders in NICU lines, CSF shunt infections indolent with low inflammatory markers, peritoneal dialysis peritonitis causes, each rewarding speciation and repeated isolation rather than single culture dismissal. Context, repetition and devices convert commensals into diagnoses.
steps.say: In NICU and shunt patients, repeated CoNS is a pathogen with paperwork.

left.title: Niche diseases
points: NICU late onset sepsis via lines
VP shunt malfunction with low grade fever
